How and when will I get my CBE grade report?

A grade report will be mailed to your school (if selected during registration process). Students may also print a copy of the grade report from the “Grades” tab inside their portal.

For full-time Texas Tech K-12 students, the CBE grade will be recorded on the student’s Texas Tech K-12 transcript.

Students who take a CBE will receive a numerical grade for the exam. No additional feedback will be provided.

Students who took a CBE through their local School (Institutional Services) should check with their school Counselor for their grades.

The teacher has 2 calendar days to post the CBE grade after the exam has been submitted/received in our office. If it has been past 2 days, please contact the teacher requesting a status of the grade.

We have received some reports of School Counselors and students not being able to access the Adobe PDF copy of the grade report. We ask that you please ensure that you are using Google Chrome and that in your extensions, that the Adobe Acrobat extension is currently enabled. We also ask that you please ensure that your current Adobe setting is set to “Covert Current web page to an Adobe PDF File has access to this site. If these settings are not enabled, we ask that you please check with your District IT to ensure that the extensions are enabled.

Benefits of the Texas Tech K-12 Supplemental Program

Step 1: Allow students to start with Texas Tech K-12 at anytime

Step 2: From the date of enrollment, students have six months (180 days) to complete the course

Step 3: Complete final exams from home with Texas Tech K-12’s proctoring service, Proctorio.

Step 4: Graduate Early or On Time: Stay on track—or get ahead—with courses that complement your current school curriculum.

Step 5: Access Advanced Placement (AP) Courses: Challenge yourself with college-level coursework that prepares you for higher education and boosts your college applications.

Step 6: Expand Your Learning Options: Enroll in courses not available at traditional schools to broaden your academic experience.

Step 7: Learn on Your Schedule: Our self-paced format fits seamlessly with your existing school schedule and commitments.

Step 8: Recover Credits: Retake courses to make up failed credits and stay on track for graduation.

Step 9: Replace Summer School: Complete required coursework during the summer without a traditional classroom setting.

Assignment Grades

Teachers have two business days to grade assignments. Plan ahead to ensure your schedule allows for this grading time. Communicate with your Texas Tech K-12 advisor (full-time students) or your local campus counselor (supplemental students) for us to work with you and help you meet deadlines for graduation, employment, and college.

Allow five business days for the course grade to be recorded before requesting a grade report. Only completed courses are officially reported and recorded. There is no academic penalty for failure to complete a course.

· How long will it take to receive a grade?

· Teachers have up to two business days after receipt in the Texas Tech K-12 office to return a grade. Grade reports are available in the Focus portal once they are posted. If your School Counselor needs a copy of the grade report, they should be able to download a copy from the Focus portal. Students that would like a hard copy should contact Texas Tech K-12 to request one be mailed. Please note that some assignments in Canvas will post grades immediately. Some assignments may require the teacher to post a grade. Please ensure that the teacher has had two business days to post the grade before contacting our office.

Conduct

You are responsible for your personal conduct and behavior. A distance education course, whether online or in print, carries the same expectations as a course in a traditional classroom. The teacher monitors and evaluates student conduct and behavior, and you will be held accountable for your words and actions.

Behavior or language not appropriate for a traditional classroom is likewise not appropriate in a Texas Tech K-12 course. This includes, but is not limited to, the use of profanity and the refusal to complete assignments. Behaving in this manner may result in being dropped from your course(s). By enrolling in a course or CBE, you have entered into an agreement with Texas Tech K-12 to refrain from the use of profanity in both written and oral communication and to behave in an appropriate and respectful manner at all times.

For further information regarding student conduct in a Texas Tech K-12 course, please read the Texas Tech K-12 Policies

Attendance/Progress Requirements for students in the Texas Tech K-12 Tuition-Free Program

The following attendance requirement applies to all full-time students who are Texas residents and who are enrolled in the tuition-free program, unless a specific exemption has been granted by a school administrator.

Step 1: In your all-online program, “attendance” will be defined as progress within each semester course.

Step 2: You will have six months (180 days from the date of enrollment) to complete each semester course.

Step 3: You must maintain enrollment in a minimum of four semester courses.

Step 4: You must complete a minimum of 5% of course assignments in every seven-day period. For example, if your course has 20 assignments, you need to complete a minimum of one per week. If your course has 60 assignments, you must average a minimum of three per week.

Step 5: Please note:

Step 6: Completing the minimum number of assignments does not guarantee you will complete within the 6-month time frame.

Step 7: Completing the minimum number of assignments and courses may not maintain your appropriate grade level or anticipated graduation date.

Step 8: If your progress is adequate, your parent may request “vacation” days. These must be requested and approved in advance.

· Exams are built behind an adaptive release in Blackboard and Canvas. Therefore, assignments must be completed and graded before the exam will be released.

Minimum Lesson/Unit Completion Requirements

Students demonstrate attendance in Texas Tech K-12 online school by regularly completing assignments. Attendance is directly tied to what the student accomplishes and/or produces over a given period. The assignments completed are the evidence that a student has been in attendance, and if no work is produced, then a student is not considered to be in attendance.

Unless specifically stated otherwise, attendance is required a minimum of 3 days per week. A student must complete at least 5% of course assignments in a seven-day period and in every subsequent seven-day period until the course is completed.

Course completion is required to earn course credit. No partial course credit will be granted. Course credit is earned when the student has successfully demonstrated mastery of the Texas Essential Knowledge and Skills for the course.

Students have six months (180 days) from the date of enrollment to complete each course. To remain in the program, students must be concurrently enrolled in a minimum of four courses.

Failure to meet minimum progress requirements may cause Texas Tech K-12 to implement truancy processes and may result in your removal from the program.

Grading and receiving results

Step 1: Print bulk exams: graded within 5 business days. Results mailed to the school/district every Friday.

Step 2: Online bulk exams: graded within 2 business days. Grades are in the portal. Grade reports mailed after certification.

Step 3: Teachers may grade at different speeds depending on volume. Substitutions and some cases may take longer. We do not release bulk Credit By Exam results directly to students or parents. Counselors can view grades in the Counselor Portal. Request access via the Support Portal if needed.

AI (artificial intelligence) use policy

Step 1: Do not use generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools such as ChatGPT or PhotoMath to do assignments or exams.

Step 2: If an instructor believes Artificial Intelligence was used, the work may get a zero. The student may need an one-on-one video check or another assignment. The highest possible score for a replacement assignment is 70%. Repeated violations may lead to removal from the program.
